title: VERIDIAN Auditor Engine Finding Record
description: Phase 0 (task-20260724-042659) design artifact. The one machine-language record shape every audit domain's output MUST conform to, regardless of which OSS tool (or AI Review pass) produced it. Enforcement mechanism (a validator wired into the pipeline) is explicitly deferred to a later phase per this task's CONSTRAINTS -- this file is the contract that later phase defines against, not yet an enforced gate.

finding_id.description: Stable unique id, e.g. 'fnd_' + ULID. Generated by the emitting tool-adapter, never hand-typed.

domain.description: Which of the 15 audit domains (or the observability layer's own self-check) this finding belongs to. Enum matches AUDITOR_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN_2026-07-24.yaml domains[].id one-for-one.

standard_cited.description: The mandatory external standard this finding is graded against (e.g. 'OWASP ASVS 4.0', 'WCAG 2.2 AA', 'ISO/IEC 25010:2023'). Must match domains[].standard_cited in the phase plan for this domain -- a finding citing a different standard than its domain's mandatory one is itself malformed.

clause_cited.description: The specific clause/rule/control id within standard_cited (e.g. 'ASVS V5.3.4', 'WCAG 1.4.3', 'CKV_DOCKER_3'). Required even when the underlying tool's own rule id is reused verbatim -- traceability to the standard, not just the tool, is the point.

artifact.description: The exact real thing the finding is about.

commit.description: git commit sha the finding was raised against, when the artifact is version-controlled

finding.description: Human-and-machine-readable statement of what was found. Never contains raw secret values -- see remediation_type=software_fixable + severity=critical convention for secret-class findings, which must reference a redacted fingerprint instead (tool-specific fingerprint field, not the plaintext).

not_covered_by_standard.description: True when this finding falls in a gap the cited standard_cited does not actually address (the standard has no clause for it) -- distinct from remediation_type. Lets the observability layer separately track 'we found something real but had to reach outside the mandatory standard to name it.' NOT_COVERED_BY_STANDARD per SCOPE item 4's exact naming.

remediation_type.description: software_fixable: a deterministic patch/config change closes this finding with no LLM judgment needed. ai_escalation_required: closing it requires human/AI judgment (design tradeoff, business-capability naming, UX content quality, etc.) -- routed to the AI Review lane, read-only against this record, never regenerating it.

producer.description: What actually generated this record -- PART5's mandatory rule: for domains with a deterministic OSS tool, this must be tool-based, never llm-based, in the audit-run path itself.

repo.description: One of the Owner's named 7 repos (MASTER_INDEX.yaml repos: block) or veda-advisors.

event_id.description: Foreign key into AUDITOR_ENGINE_EVENT_SCHEMA_2026-07-24.schema.json's event_id for the finding_emitted event that carried this record. Null only for findings authored before the event layer existed (backfill).

owner_decision_ref.description: When status handling itself required an Owner decision (e.g. a crontab change, a wont_fix on a critical), the id of the row in ai-os/OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_*.yaml.
